_comment: Email templates. Scheduled ones have arrives_turn; templates without it only arrive as follow-ups.
classification: UNCLASSIFIED | CONFIDENTIAL | SECRET | TOP SECRET
effects keys: treasury, manpower, population, morale, military_morale, tax_rate, stockpiles{}, flags{}
on_arrival: effects applied when the email is delivered (e.g. a failure report).
follow_ups: [{email, delay_weeks}] or [{delay_weeks, chance, outcomes:[{email, weight}]}]
deadline_weeks + on_expire: if unanswered by then, on_expire is applied automatically.
intel: fog-of-war estimates, referenced in body as {name}. {value|nation+stat+fraction, accuracy 0-1}

emails.sender: Gen. Aurel Vance, Chief of the Defence Staff
emails.subject: Transfer of Command — Initial Briefing
emails.body:
{leader_title},

On behalf of the Defence Staff, congratulations on your investiture. As of 0600 this morning, the terminal you are reading this on is the single point of command for the armed forces and civil administration of the {nation}.

The situation you inherit is not a comfortable one:

  - The Treasury is solvent, but only just. The previous administration financed its road programme on short-term credit.
  - Civil morale is holding. The dockyards in Port Cassel are restless over wages.
  - The officer corps is unhappy with pay and with the previous government. Do not take their loyalty for granted.
  - The Vosk Hegemony continues to mass formations near the Frontier. Their intentions are unclear.

Understand three things. If the people lose all faith in you, they will rise. If the army loses faith in you, it will act. If the Treasury runs dry for long, the state simply stops.

Your ministers will report through this inbox. Some dispatches demand a reply, and some have deadlines. Silence is also an answer.

For the Commonwealth.

— A. VANCE

emails.subject: Treasury Position at Transfer of Office
emails.body:
At transfer of office the Treasury holds 1,250,000 CR in liquid reserves. Weekly tax receipts roughly cover civil administration and armed forces pay, with a thin margin.

A negative balance incurs 1% weekly interest and leaves the armed forces unpaid. The state cannot survive more than eight consecutive weeks of insolvency.

From next week the Treasury will transmit an automated Weekly Status & Financial Report at the start of each week.

— Office of the Chancellor

emails.subject: Vosk Troop Concentrations — Frontier Sector
emails.body:
SOURCE RELIABILITY: C (fairly reliable)

Aerial reconnaissance and a single human source report Vosk infantry and at least one armored formation within 40 km of the Frontier line.

Estimated Vosk strength in sector: {vosk_frontier} men.

Rail traffic into Karzan has doubled in the last fortnight, which is consistent with stockpiling fuel and munitions.

Assessment: an exercise, or preparation for a limited offensive. Our coverage is thin, and these figures should be treated with caution.

We request authority to expand agent networks inside the Hegemony. Please respond within three weeks.

options.label: Authorize expansion of agent networks (40,000 CR)
Maintain current surveillance posture
Leak the report to the press to rally the public

on_expire.label: No direction given. The Directorate maintains its current posture.

emails.subject: Network LANTERN Operational — Revised Frontier Estimate
emails.body:
SOURCE RELIABILITY: B (usually reliable)

The expanded network, codename LANTERN, is now operational, with three sources inside the Vosk General Staff logistics directorate.

Revised estimate, Vosk strength in the Frontier sector: {vosk_frontier} men.
Estimated total Vosk mobilizable manpower: {vosk_total}.

LANTERN reports that Vosk fuel depots near the Frontier are only partially stocked. Their formations could not sustain an offensive for more than three to four weeks without resupply.

No reply required.

emails.subject: URGENT — Karzan Network Compromised
emails.body:
The expanded network has been rolled up by Vosk state security within days of activation. Three of our officers, operating under diplomatic cover, were arrested in Karzan. Vosk state radio is already announcing a public show trial for 'Kestrian imperialist spies'.

We have lost the money and the network, and the story is running in our own newspapers.

How do you wish to proceed?

options.label: Deny everything. They are private citizens.
Quietly negotiate a prisoner exchange (25,000 CR)
Retaliate: expel the entire Vosk embassy

on_expire.label: No response. The officers are tried and executed.

emails.subject: Prisoner Exchange Completed
emails.body:
The three officers crossed the bridge at Greywater at dawn, in exchange for two Vosk trade attachés we had been holding on customs charges. The press has been told it was a humanitarian gesture.

No reply required.

emails.subject: Exchange Talks Collapsed — Officers Sentenced
emails.body:
Vosk negotiators took our payment through intermediaries and then broke off contact. All three officers were sentenced to twenty years' hard labour this morning.

The officer corps is taking this badly.

No reply required.

emails.subject: Formal Protest from the Vosk Embassy
emails.body:
The Vosk ambassador delivered a formal note of protest this morning, calling our recent conduct 'a deliberate provocation' and demanding a public apology within the week.

If we apologize, the matter closes, but the press and the army will call it weakness. If we reject it, we should expect Karzan to escalate on the Frontier.

options.label: Issue a carefully worded apology
Reject the note publicly

on_expire.label: The note goes unanswered. Karzan takes this as contempt.

emails.subject: FLASH — Exchange of Fire at Frontier Post 14
emails.body:
At 0215 last night Frontier Post 14 came under small-arms and mortar fire from the Vosk side of the line. Our garrison returned fire.

Initial casualty reports, both sides combined: {casualties}. Communications with the forward posts are intermittent, and these numbers are unreliable.

The Vosk press is claiming we fired first. We do not yet know whether this was a probe, an accident, or the opening of something larger.

options.label: Reinforce the Frontier garrison (30,000 CR, 2,000 men)
Lodge a diplomatic protest and hold position
Classify the incident and suppress press coverage

on_expire.label: No orders issued. Local commanders act on their own initiative.

emails.subject: Port Cassel Dockworkers Threaten Strike
emails.body:
The Port Cassel Dockworkers' Union has issued an ultimatum: a 12% wage increase within two weeks or a general walkout.

Port Cassel handles most of our crude oil imports. A prolonged strike would choke fuel production within a month.

Awaiting your direction. The union's deadline is firm.

options.label: Meet their demands in full (60,000 CR)
Open negotiations and offer 5% (25,000 CR)
Declare the strike illegal and deploy the gendarmerie

on_expire.label: The ultimatum is ignored. The dockworkers walk out.

emails.subject: Port Cassel Agreement Signed
emails.body:
After two weeks of talks the union has accepted a compromise. The docks are working normally.

No reply required.

emails.subject: General Walkout at Port Cassel
emails.body:
The dockworkers have walked out. Tankers are anchored in the roads, unable to unload, and we have already lost one crude shipment to demurrage and spoilage.

The strike committee says it will hold out 'as long as it takes'.

options.label: Concede now, at a worse price (80,000 CR)
Send army engineers to work the docks
Wait them out

emails.subject: Casualties During Dockyard Clearance
emails.body:
Clearance of the Port Cassel dockyard met organized resistance. Gendarmes opened fire after being attacked with iron bars and petrol bombs.

Confirmed civilian dead: {dead}. Rioting has spread to the old town. Foreign journalists were present.

options.label: Declare martial law in Port Cassel
Withdraw the gendarmerie and reopen talks (60,000 CR)
Announce an independent inquiry (10,000 CR)

on_expire.label: No orders. The rioting burns itself out after three nights.

emails.subject: Blight Reported in Harrowfen Grain Belt
emails.body:
Agronomists report a fungal blight spreading through the Harrowfen lowlands. If unchecked, the projected fall in grain output for the season is {loss} percent.

Grain is the base input for military rations.

options.label: Fund emergency crop treatment (35,000 CR)
Begin civilian rationing to protect reserves
Take no action

emails.subject: Harrowfen Blight Contained
emails.body:
The blight has been contained. Yields are close to forecast, and early harvest receipts are above expectations.

No reply required.

emails.subject: Harrowfen Harvest Below Forecast
emails.body:
The blight was slowed but not stopped. Harrowfen output is down about ten percent. Reserves have been drawn on to cover the gap.

No reply required.

emails.subject: Harvest Failure in Harrowfen
emails.body:
The blight has destroyed most of the Harrowfen crop. Bread prices in {capital} rose 40% this week. There have been queues and scuffles outside bakeries.

Without intervention, reserves will not last the winter.

options.label: Import grain from abroad (90,000 CR)
Requisition grain from farmers
Let the market settle it

on_expire.label: No intervention. Bread riots in the capital.

emails.sender: Gen. Aurel Vance, Chief of the Defence Staff
emails.subject: Officer Corps Grievances — Pay and Standing
emails.body:
{leader_title},

I must be frank. Junior and field-grade officers have not had a pay rise in six years, and several regimental messes have been openly critical of the government. I have heard the word 'Council' used in ways I do not like.

I recommend visible action. Loyalty is cheaper to buy now than to restore later.

— A. VANCE

options.label: Grant a 15% officer pay rise (50,000 CR)
Medals, a victory parade, and speeches (8,000 CR)
Retire the loudest critics

emails.subject: Vosk Note Demanding Withdrawal from the Frontier
emails.body:
The Vosk Supreme Chairman has sent a note demanding that the Commonwealth withdraw all military personnel from the Frontier province within fourteen days and recognise it as 'a demilitarized zone under Vosk supervision'.

The Directorate of Military Intelligence estimates Vosk forces now massed opposite the Frontier at {vosk_massing} men. It adds that its own estimates have been wrong before.

This is the most serious crisis since the last war. Your answer will be read in Karzan and in every officers' mess in the Commonwealth.

options.label: Partial mobilization of reserves (120,000 CR, 8,000 men)
Propose talks in a neutral capital
Publicly reject the note

on_expire.label: No reply sent. Karzan reads silence as weakness.

emails.subject: Talks in Iren Produce a Framework
emails.body:
Talks in the Iren Straits have produced a framework: both sides will pull back heavy weapons 20 km from the Frontier line, with neutral observers. Nobody believes it will last, but it buys time.

No reply required.

emails.subject: Vosk Delegation Walks Out
emails.body:
The Vosk delegation walked out of the Iren talks on the second day, citing 'Kestrian bad faith'. The army sees the talks as a humiliation.

No reply required.
